staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable Little CMS snapshot in `gt_results/arvo_756/_work/src/lcms`.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow, and the staged source plus `patch.diff` close the parser-admission defect: `Type_MPE_Read()` accepts an `mpet` tag whose outer header says `8 -> 9` even though the aliased inner `clut` elements make the real pipeline `3 -> 3`. The saved ASan trace independently closes later reachability into `CLUTElemDup -> OptimizeByResampling -> EvaluateCLUTfloat -> TetrahedralInterpFloat` on a duplicated 96-byte CLUT copy. What remains unresolved is the exact source-level transition that turned the canonical duplicated `3 -> 3`, `2x2x2` interpolation state into the noncanonical sink-time state that made line 642 read 27 floats from that 24-float allocation. `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, so Stage 02 leaves that bridge explicit instead of inventing it.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4; Crash State: TetrahedralInterpFloat / _LUTevalFloat / XFormSampler16; Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: The staged 735-byte witness is a malformed ICC device-link profile whose `D2B0` tag at offset `0xe4` is an `mpet` multi-process-element value. `Type_MPE_Read()` parses attacker-controlled outer channel counts `8 -> 9`, allocates a placeholder pipeline with those endpoints, and then reads two position-table entries that both point to the same inner `clut` element at relative offset `42`. That aliased inner element declares only `3 -> 3` channels with a `2x2x2` float grid, so `ReadMPEElem()` inserts two `3 -> 3` CLUT stages and `cmsPipelineInsertStage()` / `BlessLUT()` rewrites the actual pipeline endpoints to `3 -> 3`. The vulnerable code then returns success without checking that the outer `8 -> 9` declaration still matches `NewLUT->InputChannels` / `NewLUT->OutputChannels`; the staged patch adds exactly that missing comparison and would reject this witness at parse time. Stage 01's ASan trace independently shows the admitted malformed pipeline being duplicated through `CLUTElemDup()` into a 96-byte float-table allocation and later crashing at `TetrahedralInterpFloat()` line 642 during `OptimizeByResampling()`. The staged artifacts therefore close malformed-pipeline admission and later crash reachability, but they do not preserve which additional runtime interpolation-state change turned the canonical duplicated `3 -> 3`, `2x2x2` CLUT into the noncanonical line-642 read observed by ASan.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path that materializes the multi-process-element tag's declared endpoint channel counts from attacker-controlled bytes.
source.value_from: In the staged `poc`, the `D2B0` tag's `mpet` payload starts at offset `0xe4`; bytes `00 08 00 09` at offsets `0xec..0xef` are the outer MPE header, so this statement reads `InputChans = 8` and `OutputChans = 9` from attacker-controlled profile data.

root_cause.description: Patch-matched parser-admission defect. After all MPE elements are parsed, the function returns success without checking that the attacker-declared outer channel counts still match the actual first/last stage channels stored in `NewLUT`.
root_cause.note: On the witness, the outer header is `8 -> 9` but the aliased inner `clut` element inserted twice leaves `NewLUT->InputChannels == 3` and `NewLUT->OutputChannels == 3`. The staged patch adds `if (InputChans != NewLUT->InputChannels || OutputChans != NewLUT->OutputChannels) goto Error;` immediately before this success return. This establishes why the malformed devicelink survives parsing, but the saved artifacts do not preserve the later source-level transition from that admitted pipeline to the exact noncanonical interpolation state that produced ASan's 27-float line-642 read.

sink.code: c2 = DENS(X1, Y1, Z1) - DENS(X1, Y0, Z1);
sink.description: ASan sink. One of the line-642 tetrahedral float CLUT reads lands outside the duplicated 96-byte heap buffer allocated for that CLUT copy.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 4` at `src/cmsintrp.c:642:22` on address `0x60800000040c`, which is 12 bytes past the duplicated 96-byte region `[0x6080000003a0, 0x608000000400)`. That is 27 floats from the allocation base, whereas source proves a canonical unshifted duplicate of the parsed `3 -> 3`, `2x2x2` CLUT would stay within indices `0..23`. This GT therefore closes the admitted malformed CLUT copy plus the witnessed sink, but leaves the exact sink-time interpolation-state deviation explicit and unresolved.

tainted_value_origin.description: The same attacker-controlled `mpet` position table supplies both element offsets. On the witness, both records decode to relative offset `42`, so the parser seeks to the same inner `clut` element twice.

parser_admitted.description: The malformed profile has already been accepted as a float devicelink profile with a `D2B0` tag, and Little CMS is now duplicating the parsed MPE pipeline for transform construction instead of rejecting the tag earlier.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` requested tighter sink-state grounding, but `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` disabled and the reviewer did not request the bounded measurement path (`needs_runtime_disambiguation` is false). Stage 02 therefore repaired the trace using only staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, the reproduction report, and static parsing of the staged `poc` bytes.

The staged PoC bytes let Stage 02 prove the parser defect precisely: the `D2B0` `mpet` header declares outer channels `8 -> 9`, both position-table entries alias the same inner `clut` at relative offset `42`, and that inner `clut` declares only `3 -> 3` channels with a `2x2x2` grid. Source also proves that duplicating that CLUT normally yields `nSamples=[2,2,2]`, `Domain=[1,1,1]`, `nOutputs=3`, and `opta=[3,6,12]`, which would bound an unshifted line-642 lookup to indices `0..23`.

What Stage 01 artifacts do not preserve is the additional runtime deviation that made ASan observe address `0x60800000040c` (27 floats from the duplicated allocation base) at the sink. Stage 02 therefore treats this sample as intentionally partial: the parser-admission bug and the later crashing CLUT copy are source-grounded, but the exact sink-time interpolation-state mutation remains unresolved.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed build, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing post-parse channel-consistency check described at the root-cause step.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness opens the staged malformed ICC profile with `cmsOpenProfileFromMem()` and then calls `cmsCreateTransform()` on the parsed source profile and an sRGB destination profile.

While parsing the source profile's `D2B0` `mpet` tag, Little CMS reads outer MPE channels `8 -> 9`, follows two aliased directory entries to the same inner `3 -> 3` `clut`, rewrites the real pipeline endpoints to `3 -> 3`, and still returns success without checking the outer/inner mismatch.

Transform construction treats the admitted `D2B0` value as a float devicelink LUT, duplicates it, and later sees only the rewritten `3 -> 3` pipeline endpoints, so the malformed devicelink is not rejected before optimization.

While linking the transform, `CLUTElemDup()` duplicates a 96-byte float table for the malformed CLUT and rebuilds the duplicated `cmsInterpParams` object from that stage's dimensions and output count.
During transform allocation, the optimizer resamples the linked pipeline and feeds sampled float inputs plus the duplicated CLUT state into `EvaluateCLUTfloat -> TetrahedralInterpFloat`.

At line 642, one of the tetrahedral CLUT reads lands 27 floats from the duplicated allocation base; source proves a canonical unshifted `3 -> 3`, `2x2x2` duplicate would only permit indices `0..23`, so the final sink-driving interpolation-state deviation remains unobserved in Stage 01 artifacts.

fine_trace.code:
if (!_cmsReadUInt16Number(io, &InputChans)) return NULL;
    if (!_cmsReadUInt16Number(io, &OutputChans)) return NULL;
fine_trace.note: Source. The MPE parser reads the outer endpoint declaration from attacker-controlled profile bytes. In the staged witness, these two reads materialize `InputChans = 8` and `OutputChans = 9` from the `D2B0` tag's `mpet` header.
The parser allocates an empty pipeline placeholder whose endpoint counts come directly from the attacker-declared outer header, so `NewLUT` initially carries the malformed `8 -> 9` channel contract.
The same tag next declares there are two MPE directory entries. On the witness, this read yields `ElementCount = 2`.

The MPE directory records are read from attacker-controlled bytes. For this witness, both entries decode to the same relative offset `42`, so after adding `BaseOffset` they both resolve to absolute offset `0x10e` and the parser will visit the same inner element twice.

fine_trace.code:
if (!_cmsReadUInt16Number(io, &InputChans)) return NULL;
    if (!_cmsReadUInt16Number(io, &OutputChans)) return NULL;
fine_trace.note: At the aliased inner element offset `0x10e`, the element reader materializes a `clut` stage with only `3 -> 3` channels. This is the first concrete mismatch against the outer `8 -> 9` header from step 1.

fine_trace.code: mpe = cmsStageAllocCLutFloatGranular(self ->ContextID, GridPoints, InputChans, OutputChans, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Using the inner `3 -> 3` declaration and the staged witness's first three dimension bytes `[2, 2, 2]` (later dimension bytes are ignored because `InputChans = 3`), the parser allocates a 3D float CLUT stage. That stage's table has `3 * 2 * 2 * 2 = 24` float entries, which becomes the 96-byte buffer ASan later attributes to `CLUTElemDup()`.

Both aliased directory entries from step 4 execute this insertion path, so the same `3 -> 3` CLUT element is inserted twice. `cmsPipelineInsertStage()` immediately calls `BlessLUT()`, which rewrites the pipeline's actual endpoints from the outer placeholder `8 -> 9` to the inserted stages' first/last channels `3 -> 3`.

Root cause. After all elements are parsed, `Type_MPE_Read()` returns success without checking that the outer header from step 1 still matches the actual pipeline endpoints from step 7. On the witness, the function therefore accepts an `mpet` tag whose declared contract is `8 -> 9` but whose real pipeline is `3 -> 3`.

Transform construction treats the admitted `D2B0` tag as a float devicelink LUT and duplicates the accepted pipeline returned at step 8. The witness header carries `Lab ` as both source color space and PCS, so this helper then wraps that pipeline with Lab-normalization stages without rechecking the outer `8 -> 9` MPE declaration.

While `_cmsLinkProfiles()` concatenates the devicelink into the transform pipeline, the malformed CLUT stage is duplicated into a fresh float-table allocation. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this exact `_cmsDupMem()` call as the source of the 96-byte region `[0x6080000003a0, 0x608000000400)` later read out of bounds.

fine_trace.code:
NewElem ->Params   = _cmsComputeInterpParamsEx(mpe ->ContextID,
                                                   Data ->Params ->nSamples,
                                                   Data ->Params ->nInputs,
                                                   Data ->Params ->nOutputs,
                                                   NewElem ->Tab.T,
                                                   Data ->Params ->dwFlags);
fine_trace.note: The duplicate rebuilds its interpolation state from the original stage's dimensions and output count. For the parsed CLUT from step 6, this source path yields the canonical duplicate `nSamples=[2,2,2]`, `Domain=[1,1,1]`, `nOutputs=3`, and `opta=[3,6,12]`, all pointing at the 24-float copy from step 10. On its own, that state would bound an unshifted line-642 lookup to indices `0..23`, so ASan's 27-float access implies some later sink-time deviation that the saved artifacts do not record.

After `_cmsLinkProfiles()` returns, transform construction performs the last structural guard before `AllocEmptyTransform()`. The witness is not rejected here because the admitted devicelink now presents as `3 -> 3`, matching the source profile's `Lab` colorspace and the 3-channel sRGB destination path, even though the original outer `mpet` header declared `8 -> 9`.

Because step 12 does not reject the linked transform, `AllocEmptyTransform()` runs optimizer resampling and evaluates the linked pipeline by iterating a 16-bit destination CLUT through `XFormSampler16 -> cmsPipelineEvalFloat`. The saved ASan stack confirms that this exact resampling path reaches the duplicated float CLUT copy.

The duplicated CLUT copy from steps 10 and 11 is evaluated on the optimizer path. The saved ASan stack closes `XFormSampler16 -> cmsPipelineEvalFloat -> _LUTevalFloat -> EvaluateCLUTfloat -> TetrahedralInterpFloat`, but it does not preserve which sink-time `p->Table`, `p->opta[]`, `p->nOutputs`, or equivalent interpolation state differed from the canonical duplicate summarized at step 11.
The crashing execution took the `rx >= rz && rz >= ry` tetrahedral arm, because ASan pinpoints line 642 inside this branch.

fine_trace.code: c2 = DENS(X1, Y1, Z1) - DENS(X1, Y0, Z1);
fine_trace.note: Sink. ASan proves one of the line-642 `DENS(...)` reads on the duplicated 96-byte table from step 10 landed at address `0x60800000040c`, i.e. 108 bytes or 27 floats from the allocation base `0x6080000003a0`. Step 11 shows the canonical duplicated state reconstructed from source would only permit unshifted indices `0..23`, so Stage 02 can close reachability from the admitted malformed CLUT copy to this sink but not the exact additional source-level transition that made the sink-time interpolation state noncanonical.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. The patch-relevant parse bug at step 8 admits the malformed `D2B0` pipeline that step 10 later duplicates through `CLUTElemDup()`, so it is the established source-level admission defect behind the crashing CLUT copy. The saved artifacts do not preserve which extra interpolation-state change inside that admitted pipeline made the final line-642 read reach float index 27.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved ASan stack matches the observed later path `TetrahedralInterpFloat -> EvaluateCLUTfloat -> _LUTevalFloat -> cmsPipelineEvalFloat -> XFormSampler16 -> OptimizeByResampling -> AllocEmptyTransform -> cmsCreateExtendedTransform`, while the earlier parser/admission half is grounded in the staged vulnerable source plus static parsing of the staged `poc` bytes. The GT now marks the missing sink-time interpolation-state bridge as intentionally unresolved rather than claiming it is closed.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially closed. The witness bytes set the outer `8 -> 9` header and aliased `mpet` directory entries that make `Type_MPE_Read()` return an admitted malformed `D2B0` pipeline, and the crashing stack later duplicates and evaluates a CLUT copy from that admitted pipeline. What remains unresolved is the exact additional source-level transition from the canonical duplicated `3 -> 3`, `2x2x2` state to the noncanonical interpolation state used at the sink.

poc.trigger: Open the staged ICC profile with `cmsOpenProfileFromMem()` and call `cmsCreateTransform(srcProfile, srcFormat, dstProfile, TYPE_BGR_8, 0, 0)`. Transform construction parses the malformed `D2B0` `mpet` tag, links the accepted float devicelink pipeline, and crashes during `OptimizeByResampling()` before `cmsDoTransform()` is reached.

format.name: ICC device-link profile
format.contract: The staged 735-byte witness contains a `D2B0` tag at offset `0xe4` whose `mpet` payload declares outer MPE channels `8 -> 9`, `ElementCount = 2`, and two position-table entries that both point to the same inner `clut` element at relative offset `42`. That inner `clut` element declares `3 -> 3` channels with a `2x2x2` float grid.
